body.en:
Find the volume of a cube of side \( 4 \).

\[ 4^{3}=64. \]

Find the volume of a cylinder with \( r=2 \), \( h=5 \). Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ \pi r^{2}h=3.14\times 4\times 5=62.8. \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Cones and Pyramids Have a 1/3 Factor

body.en: A notorious test trap is forgetting the \( \tfrac{1}{3} \) factor for solids that taper to an apex (cones and pyramids): \( V = \tfrac{1}{3} B h \). A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder holds exactly one-third the volume. Also take care with surface area vs volume units: volume is in cubic units (\( \text{cm}^3 \)), surface area is in square units (\( \text{cm}^2 \)).

label.en: Worked Example C — Euclidean Distance & Orthogonal Projection

body.en:
A displacement has horizontal component \( \Delta x = 4 \) and vertical component \( \Delta y = 9 \). Find the squared magnitude \( d^2 \) and the area of the right triangle formed with the axes.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. By the Pythagorean theorem, \( d^2 = (4)^2 + (9)^2 = 16 + 81 = \mathbf{97} \).
  2. The enclosed right-triangle area is \( A = \frac{1}{2}(4)(9) = \mathbf{18} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Euclidean Distance & Orthogonal Projection

body.en:
A displacement has horizontal component \( \Delta x = 5 \) and vertical component \( \Delta y = 5 \). Find the squared magnitude \( d^2 \) and the area of the right triangle formed with the axes.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. By the Pythagorean theorem, \( d^2 = (5)^2 + (5)^2 = 25 + 25 = \mathbf{50} \).
  2. The enclosed right-triangle area is \( A = \frac{1}{2}(5)(5) = \mathbf{12.5} \).

question.en: A cone and a cylinder have identical base radii of \( 6\ \text{cm} \). If both solids have the same volume of \( 180\pi\ \text{cm}^3 \), find the height of the cylinder and the height of the cone.

solution.en:
Solution: The base area for both solids is \( B = \pi r^2 = \pi (6^2) = 36\pi\ \text{cm}^2 \).

For the cylinder:

\[ V_{\text{cyl}} = B \cdot h_{\text{cyl}} \implies 180\pi = 36\pi \cdot h_{\text{cyl}} \implies h_{\text{cyl}} = \frac{180\pi}{36\pi} = 5\ \text{cm}. \]

For the cone:

\[ V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3} B \cdot h_{\text{cone}} \implies 180\pi = \frac{1}{3} (36\pi) \cdot h_{\text{cone}} = 12\pi \cdot h_{\text{cone}} \implies h_{\text{cone}} = \frac{180\pi}{12\pi} = 15\ \text{cm}. \]

The cylinder has height \( 5\ \text{cm} \) and the cone has height \( 15\ \text{cm} \) (three times as tall to achieve equal volume).

question.en: A solid metal sphere of radius \(3\ \text{cm}\) is melted down and recast into a cylinder of radius \(2\ \text{cm}\). What is the height of the recast cylinder in cm?

solution.en:
Step 1: Calculate the volume of the sphere:

\[ V_{\text{sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi\text{ cm}^3. \]

Step 2: Equate with the volume of the cylinder:

\[ V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi R^2 h = \pi (2^2) h = 4\pi h. \]

Step 3: Solve for height \(h\):

\[ 4\pi h = 36\pi \implies h = \frac{36\pi}{4\pi} = 9\text{ cm}. \]

The height of the cylinder is \(9\) cm.

question.en: [Area, Surface Area & Volume · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Area, Surface Area & Volume · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
